data.title: Run the night, not just the RSVP.
data.lead: A pace group, a seating plan and a group walking to the next bar are different jobs. Catch knows which one you’re running, does its work in the gaps, and leaves people to enjoy the room.

data.title: Follow one evening, start to finish.

items.label: Run clubs
items.title: Sunday Social Run
items.sub: Carter Road Runners · Carter Road, Bandra
items.body: People are moving, so phones stay in pockets. Catch does its work before the start and after the finish.

list.b: Every booking brings a pace. Catch builds groups of six to eight at a similar pace, and spreads newcomers so no group is all strangers.

list.h: Check in, then pocket the phone
list.b: Runners tap in at the fountain and see their group and its lead once. After the start, Catch goes quiet: no prompts while anyone is running.

list.h: A first hello at the start line
list.b: Each group gets one question to answer together before they set off, so the first kilometre already has a conversation in it.
Group leads mark runners back at the finish. Anyone not back ten minutes after their group shows up on your screen, with their group and last check-in.
Finishers get the photos and a one-tap “same time next week?”. Anyone who asked for a steadier pace starts in a steadier group next time.

items.label: Dinners
items.title: Long Table Supper
items.body: Phones are within reach all evening, and the point is to leave them there. Catch sets the table, then gets out of the way.

list.h: Tables planned from what people told you
list.b: Applications bring who’s coming and why. Catch suggests tables of six with something in common and someone new, and you adjust with a drag.

list.h: One look at the phone, then dinner
list.b: Guests check in and see their seat once. After that, nothing at dinner needs a phone, and Catch won’t ask for one.

list.h: The whole room at a glance
list.b: The seating map shows who’s where. Seat a late arrival or move someone with a tap, and table sizes and anyone you’ve kept apart still hold.
Between courses, Catch suggests a dessert swap so everyone meets a few more people. One table gone quiet? Send it a conversation card.
Guests say who they’d happily sit with again. The people who’d come back hear about the next date first.

items.label: Games and quizzes
items.title: Tuesday Trivia Night
items.sub: Lantern Lane Social · Harbour Room, Bandra West
items.body: Heads are down during rounds and up between them. Catch only speaks in the gaps, and keeps the scores honest.

list.h: Fair teams before the first question
list.b: Catch builds teams of five from who’s coming: people on their own spread across teams, friends kept together if they asked, and no team stacked with regulars.

list.h: A team for everyone at the door
list.b: Guests check in and see their team and table. Anyone who came alone is introduced to their team by name before round one.
Between rounds, one person from each team moves on. Only the people moving get a buzz; everyone else stays in the game.
The quizmaster enters each round’s scores. Teams see their own; the leaderboard stays hidden until the end, so the last round still matters.
A countdown on every phone and the big screen at once, then the final standings. The winners pick next week’s theme.

items.label: Pickleball
items.title: Pickleball Social
items.sub: Dink and Drink · Andheri West · 40 players, 3 courts
items.body: Forty players, three courts. Phones come out between games, and Catch makes sure everyone gets their share of court time.

list.b: Each booking brings a skill level. Catch plans the rounds so every match is close and all forty players get about the same time on court.
Players confirm their level at the door. Walk-ins join the next round, not a queue.
Between games, phones buzz with the next court and partner. Nobody plays with the same partner twice until they’ve played with everyone at their level.
Catch counts every player’s minutes on court. Anyone falling behind goes on next; anyone sitting out is pointed to the lounge, and to someone there to meet.
Final standings go out with the photos. Players who want an easier or tougher session get that invitation next.

items.label: Pub crawls
items.title: Friday Bandra Pub Crawl
items.sub: Night Shift Socials · four stops in Bandra
items.body: The night moves, so the plan has to travel with it. Phones come out between stops, and Catch keeps count of everyone along the way.

list.b: Four stops, two groups of ten and a lead for each, shared with your team and the venues before the night.

list.h: A first hello at the first bar
list.b: Guests check in and get one icebreaker to do with someone in their group, so the group is mixing before the first move.
Phones come out on the move: where you’re heading and who’s with you. Each lead confirms who left and who arrived.
Someone arriving late gets the stop you’re at now, not the first one, and their lead sees them coming.
At the last stop, leads mark everyone as home or still out. Anyone not accounted for shows up on your screen.

data.title: About running the night.
items: Can I choose which activities guests see?
Yes. Pick the format and tools when you set up an event, and adjust groups or override assignments from the live console. Introductions, prompts and group activities are optional.
Do my guests need to download an app?
No. Guests join live moments in their phone’s browser after a quick phone check, with no app or profile needed.
What if my format isn’t one of these five?
Pick an open format and choose the tools you want: check-in, groups, prompts and messages work for any kind of night.
What can my team see on the night?
Your team uses the booking and application information guests provide for the event, with access suited to each role.
